opus.why: Mechanical SRT-to-VTT conversion with clear rewrap rules; high effort so the line-length and two-line limits get checked.

fable.why: Mechanical SRT→VTT conversion and 42-char re-wrap is a small script with a count to report; no production code.

opus.why: Fully specified mechanical rename that the typecheck verifies; it changes code but doesn't investigate it.

fable.why: Well-specified rename across src/ and tests/ with typecheck as the safety net; a change, not an investigation, so no prod rule.

opus.why: Trivial JSON-to-CSV flatten with exact column and format rules.

fable.why: Trivial JSON-to-CSV flatten with a fixed column spec; one short script and a two-item reply.

opus.why: A code review gating a production merge, so the owner rule sets the floor at opus high, even though the check itself is mostly grep.

fable.why: Task is a grep-level check, but it is a code review of a production-app commit, so the owner rule sets opus high as the floor.

opus.why: Read-only code search and mapping of flag reads, not debugging or review; Sonnet traces server and client reads reliably.

fable.why: Read-only usage map of one flag; needs some tracing through helpers but is a lookup, not debugging or review of production code.

opus.why: Summarising internal logs: counting, grouping errors, a median calculation and light judgment on what to look into.

fable.why: Internal log aggregation over ~40 files; scripting counts and median is easy, high effort so it normalizes error messages and does not stop early.

opus.why: Multi-source web lookup with a citation for every number and conflicts shown, but it ends in a table, not a deep-research document.

fable.why: Multi-source web research needing official pages, a URL per number and reconciliation of disagreements; sonnet high handles this, not hours-long so no fable.

opus.why: Internal code search that must follow calls through wrappers and cross-check cron and the Makefile; high effort avoids missed callers.

fable.why: Internal scripts only; tracing calls through wrappers plus cron/Makefile liveness needs modest reasoning, well scoped.

opus.why: Production money-path review covering idempotency, concurrency, rounding and ledger balance; subtle bugs justify xhigh.

fable.why: Production money-path review covering idempotency, rounding, over-refund and concurrency with ledger balance; hardest kind of review, worth above the opus-high floor.

opus.why: Security review of production session handling (fixation, rotation race, logout); opus high is enough, Fable not needed.

fable.why: Security review of production session middleware (fixation, rotation race, cookie flags, logout); owner floor applies and high effort covers it.

opus.why: Billed as quick, but it is an online migration on a huge production table: locking, backfill and rolling-deploy compatibility need real expertise.

fable.why: Sounds small but is online-migration safety on a tens-of-millions-row production table plus rolling-deploy compatibility; needs real DB locking reasoning.

opus.why: Security review of a production login rate limiter: client-IP trust, fail-open vs fail-closed, lockout abuse.

fable.why: Production auth rate-limiter review with boundary logic, proxy header trust, fail-open/closed and lockout attack; owner floor is opus high.

opus.why: Billed as a quick look, but it is a rare production race condition that needs root-causing and a concurrent repro; hard debugging.

fable.why: Intermittent double-booking race in production code, with a local concurrent repro; long agentic debugging where xhigh pays.

opus.why: Production webhook signature debugging (raw body vs middleware order) plus a safe replay plan.

fable.why: Production webhook signature failure debugging with strong clues (body-parser reorder, logs); opus high suffices to find the raw-body cause and 30% pattern.

opus.why: Production OOM root cause across streams, buffers and caches, with a local load test and a patch; long, hard investigation.

fable.why: Production OOM root-cause with heap snapshots, local load test and a patch; multi-hour agentic investigation justifies xhigh.

opus.why: Production timezone bug traced end to end, plus a judgment on whether stored data is corrupted.

fable.why: Production timezone bug traced end to end across client, API, storage and email, plus a data-corruption verdict; owner floor applies.

opus.why: Practical bug review of an internal script (error handling, Windows paths); doesn't need Opus.

fable.why: Internal script review for bugs, swallowed errors and Windows path issues; sonnet high finds these well and the brief caps scope at five issues.

opus.why: Well-known shell quoting/word-splitting fix in an internal script, tested on a scratch folder.

fable.why: Classic shell word-splitting fix in an internal script with a scratch-folder test; standard pattern, well specified.

opus.why: Docs written from repo files, matching the existing README's tone; routine content work.

fable.why: Docs writing grounded in repo files and matching existing tone; content creation is sonnet's lane and the inputs are enumerated.

opus.why: Creative writing for 14 slides in a set brand voice, grounded in the strategy doc; Sonnet high handles it well.

fable.why: Voice-matched creative writing for 14 slides constrained to a strategy doc; sonnet high matches opus on this kind of content work at lower cost.

opus.why: Spreadsheet cleanup with clear rules. Parsing durations and merging duplicates takes some judgment, but it is routine work.

fable.why: Scripted xlsx cleanup with duration parsing and merge-by-completeness logic; sonnet handles openpyxl data wrangling reliably, haiku risks botching the dedupe rule.

opus.why: Research across docs and open issues on six criteria, written up as a finished ADR. This is the research-to-document work where Fable pays.

fable.why: Multi-step research across three libraries' docs and issue trackers carried to a finished ADR decision; this is the deep-research-to-document case where fable pays.

opus.why: Research from several sources, weighed against our own setup and written as a finished, cited recommendation. The topic is well covered, so medium effort is enough.

fable.why: Reads OWASP, RFCs and engineering write-ups, weighs them against the app's auth setup, and delivers a finished cited recommendation with migration path; deep research to document.

opus.why: Long investigation of a production email problem: DNS, bounce data, provider rules and template history, ranked by evidence into a finished plan.

fable.why: Hours-long multi-source investigation of a production deliverability problem (DNS, exports, provider docs, commit history) ranked by evidence into a finished plan; fable territory and above the opus-high floor.

opus.why: Writing tests, not investigating. Telling a real bug apart from normal Intl/locale formatting differences needs care.

fable.why: Well-specified unit tests for one function with explicit case list; sonnet at medium writes and runs vitest cases correctly and can spot a real bug.

opus.why: Small, well-scoped feature: a validated query param, ordering in the repo query, and route tests.

fable.why: Scoped feature across route, repo query and tests with validation; sonnet is sufficient, high effort so it pushes ordering into the query and matches the error shape exactly.

opus.why: Minimal fix for a known edge-case bug in an internal script, plus a regression test.

fable.why: Diagnosed bug in an internal Python script with a minimal fix and regression test; routine for sonnet, haiku may miss the edge case.

opus.why: Add a flag to an internal script, cover both write paths, and write a mocked test. Standard work.

fable.why: Add a flag following existing argparse style, cover both code paths, mock-based test; internal tool, sonnet medium does this well.

opus.why: Run one command and report results in a fixed format. No fixing involved.

fable.why: Run one command and report structured results, no judgment needed; haiku low is enough.

opus.why: Short README for a small CLI, written from reading two files. Simple documentation.

fable.why: Read two small files and write a short README with strict content rules; haiku at high follows the checklist and notices undocumented bits.

opus.why: Second attempt at a data-safety-critical migration. Every call site must be found and the backfill must be correct, so step up from the model that failed.

fable.why: Retry after a data-loss mistake; backfill SQL, schema change and every call site across src and admin API must be right, so opus high despite being a change not an investigation.

opus.why: Mechanical checks of files against a spec: existence, dimensions, names, alpha channel. Needs care but little reasoning.

fable.why: Mechanical file checks but needs a small script for PNG dimensions and alpha channel; sonnet low does it without skipping checks.

opus.why: Final creative script with tight rules: cited facts, runtime target, voice guide. It goes nearly straight to the narrator, so quality matters.

fable.why: Final narrator-ready script with runtime, citation, persona and read-aloud constraints; creative quality with tight compliance needs opus, no research component to justify fable.

opus.why: Brief too short to say more. The likely task is running the test suite and reporting results, which is mechanical.

fable.why: Brief too short to know what is expected on failure; parent is opus on the production webapp, so match the parent's likely tier.

opus.why: Brief too short to say more. Likely means running the linter and fixing what it can't auto-fix in internal code, which may need small code edits.

fable.why: Brief too short to say whether this is autofix or manual lint cleanup; parent is sonnet on an internal project, so match that tier.

opus.why: Read the git diff and log and summarize them. Not a review or investigation.

fable.why: Read git log and diff, summarize in five bullets; haiku medium is adequate.

opus.why: Debugging an internal shell script, likely pipes, set -e or exit-code handling. Moderate reasoning.

fable.why: Shell exit-status diagnosis on an internal script (likely pipefail or masked status); quick for sonnet, haiku might guess wrong.

opus.why: Find code and return paths with line numbers. No debugging or review.

fable.why: Code search returning paths and line numbers, no analysis; haiku medium handles grep-and-read exploration.

opus.why: Search across files, but matches split across lines and inside pptx XML need more care than a plain grep.

fable.why: Phrase may be split across lines and across XML text runs in pptx notes, and slide numbers must be mapped; needs more care than plain grep.

opus.why: Debugging a race condition in production payment code across three paths. Production investigation needs at least Opus at high.

fable.why: Production race-condition and idempotency investigation across three code paths plus DB constraints; prod rule requires opus high minimum and concurrency tracing justifies xhigh.
